chunks: Hamzah ibn Muhammad al-Alawi (mercy of God be upon him) said: Ali ibn Ibrahim informed us, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he said:

Among the attributes of the Eternal is that He is One, Unique, Self-Sufficient, Unique in meaning, and not [subject to] many different meanings. He said: I said to him, 'May I be your ransom.' A group of Iraqis claim that He hears with something other than what He sees, and sees with something other than what He hears. He said: 'They have lied, apostatized, and anthropomorphized. Exalted is Allah from that. Verily, He is All-Hearing, All-Seeing. He hears with what He sees, and sees with what He hears.' I said: 'They claim that He is All-Seeing as they understand it.' He said: 'Exalted is Allah. Verily, [human] understanding applies only to that which has the attributes of created beings, and Allah is not like that.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Shia theological view on whether God's hearing and seeing are separate attributes?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) refutes the anthropomorphic view that God’s hearing and seeing are separate faculties, affirming instead that He is 'Ahadi al-Ma'na' (One in essence/meaning) without multiplicity. The Imam clarifies that while God is 'Sami' and 'Basir', these attributes are not composed of distinct parts as humans understand them, but are unified in His unique essence, transcending human conceptualization. This highlights the Shia doctrine of divine simplicity against the Mu'tazila and others who might over-analyze or simplify divine attributes.
